title: protect_response with include_piv=true bypasses durable sender sequence reservation
description:
The new protect_response method (lib.rs:975) with include_piv=true directly calls self.sender_seq.fetch_increment() on line 991 without going through reserve_sender/store.compare_exchange. This bypasses the durable storage protocol required by RFC 8613 - the sender sequence is incremented in memory but never atomically committed via the SenderStateStore.

If a crash occurs after encryption but before the caller manually persists the new sequence, a subsequent restore would reuse the same sequence number, compromising AES-CCM confidentiality via nonce reuse.

Fix: Either:
a) Make protect_response require a ReservedSender (restore old pattern)
b) Add a SenderStateStore parameter and integrate atomic reservation
c) Document this as a convenience wrapper and ensure all production callers use reserve_sender + protect_response_with_piv
